title: Strategy & Decision Making Adventure 1: Porter's 5 Forces
welcome_lead: Today you'll dissect industry attractiveness with Michael Porter's 5 Forces (1979).
meta_desc: IBDP Business Management Strategy: Porter's five forces — rivalry, entrants, substitutes, buyers, suppliers.
final_note: You analysed an industry with Porter's five competitive forces.

concepts.def: Intensity of competition among existing firms
Ease for new firms to enter
Customers' ability to push price down
Suppliers' ability to push price up
Patent, brand, scale that blocks rivals

walkthroughs.body_html:
Michael Porter identified five forces shaping industry profit.

1. Rivalry among existing firms.
2. Threat of new entrants.
3. Threat of substitutes.
4. Bargaining power of buyers.
5. Bargaining power of suppliers.

The stronger the forces, the lower industry profit. A weak set of forces = attractive industry.

High barriers to entry shield profit: patents, brand, scale, regulation, network effects.

Rivalry is fierce when many similar firms compete on price, growth is slow, or exit barriers are high (e.g. steel mills).

Buyer power rises when buyers are few, switching costs are low, or products are undifferentiated.

Supplier power rises when suppliers are concentrated, inputs are unique, or switching to another supplier is costly.

Apple uses brand to weaken buyer power; OPEC uses concentration to raise supplier power.
